speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) whether the wage growth is moving in tandem with productivity gains; (b) whether the sectoral wage growth is commensurate with sectoral productivity gains; (c) which sectors are productivity laggards; and (d) whether the targeted help provided has led to productivity and wage gains.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Over the long term, real wage growth should track productivity growth in order to be sustainable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This is because if real wage growth outstrips productivity growth for an extended period, businesses will be at risk of losing their competitiveness and potentially be forced to scale back or close their operations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Over the past two decades, real wages have grown broadly in tandem with productivity at the overall economy level.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In recent years, however, real wage growth has outstripped productivity growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In particular, domestically-oriented sectors like Construction and Other Services Industries saw real wages rise faster than productivity between 2011 and 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: This was, in part, due to labour market tightness, which had led to upward pressures on wages and also weak or negative productivity growth in these sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Meanwhile, even though the sluggish global economic environment had weighed on the productivity performance of outward-oriented sectors over this period, real wage growth in these sectors was generally still supported by positive productivity growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Indeed, in sectors, such as Manufacturing, Wholesale Trade and Finance & Insurance, real wages rose in tandem with productivity on the back of their relatively strong productivity performance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: However, in other sectors, such as Transportation & Storage and Accommodation, real wage growth exceeded productivity growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Against this backdrop, it is crucial that we press on with our productivity drive in order to maintain our competitiveness globally, while enabling continued improvement of Singaporeans' wages and living standards.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: In this regard, we are taking a targeted, sector-specific approach to raising productivity through the Industry Transformation Maps (ITMs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For example, under the Hotel ITM, the Singapore Tourism Board and Singapore Hotel Association have launched the Hotel Innovation Challenge to crowd-source innovative technologies that can improve hotels’ productivity and enhance the guest experience, such as facial recognition check-in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Government has also provided assistance to firms through schemes designed to help them enhance their capability and productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: These schemes have seen some early signs of success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Similarly, firms that tapped on the SMEs Go Digital programme, formerly known as iSPRINT, for IT solutions to automate their business functions between 2010 and 2013 experienced a 3.1% increase in their revenue on average over time.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: Maintaining a close partnership with industry and unions is also important in order for businesses and their workers to benefit from productivity improvements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: For example, NTUC has partnered various companies on measures that raise their productivity and competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The resultant productivity gains are then shared with the workers in these companies, such as through allowances or payments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: As a specific example, the Inclusive Growth Programme (IGP) administered by e2i co-funds companies to embark on productivity improvement projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The companies are, in turn, required to share the productivity gains with their workers through a rise in wages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Trade and Industry)
text: The Government is committed to continue to work with businesses and the unions to help businesses improve their productivity and ensure that the productivity gains are shared with workers through higher wages.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Speaker, I would like to thank the Senior Minister of State for the answer.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am glad to know that the real wage growth is 1.9% and productivity growth is 1.1%.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I would just like to ask a couple of supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: First, in terms of MTI, can the Senior Minister of State share a bit more about the productivity or wage growth outlook over the next few years?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Yesterday, I had asked about the concerns if interest rates were to go up over the next year or so and what it would mean for wage growth outlook from MTI's perspective.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The second question is about concerns on the ground about wage stagnation.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As the Senior Minister of State mentioned, the outlook for wage growth is that it would not be broad-based growth.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How do you allay some of the wage stagnation concerns for specific sectors?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As what the Senior Minister of State had mentioned, some sectors are affected more than others.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I think the key is that wage growth will not be uniform across all sectors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Fundamental to driving sustainable wage growth would be to improve productivity.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It is one of the important tenets of the ITMs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We want to help our companies to better increase productivity by leveraging on technology such that the companies can make better profit margins while controlling their costs from various pressures.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: An example of how we can help some of these wage gains translate to benefits from the workers' wages would be in programmes like the IGPs.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But importantly, you also need to put in place a lot of framework to help our workers re-skill and upskill so that they can be productive.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Individual workers can leverage on this skills framework to continue to upskill themselves, working with the employers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The other scheme which the Government has put forth is the WorkPro Job Redesign grant.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Because this is the group where there is probably genuine concern about wage stagnation and also job prospects.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: By using such schemes and grants, we can encourage companies to help level up the workers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And, in turn, companies can benefit from having more experienced workers, especially higher productivity ones.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We do see that there is a need to do more for other sectors.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: NTUC has announced recently that the Labour Movement has begun conducting surveys with F&B workers as part of early efforts to see if this can be included in the Progressive Wage Model as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, there are multiple approaches but, fundamentally, they all hinge on raising the productivity of our workers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Which sectors does the Senior Minister of State think will be affected most in the next three to five years?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We do see that certain sectors would have a lot more chances for manpower growth in terms of number of jobs created.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The wages in these growth sectors will probably be a lot more competitive as well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It includes sectors that deal with commodity trading, but also trading in many other areas.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, in the logistics sector, which is also a key sector in this group.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The other growth sector would be in the manufacturing space.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For example, precision engineering and the semi-conductor industry are still continuing to do well.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, these are the areas in which I think workers would continue to see specific gains.
